chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The generous one is close to Allah, close to Paradise, and close to the people.' And I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Generosity is a tree in Paradise; whoever holds onto one of its branches will enter Paradise.'

key_terms.السَّخِيُّ: The generous person (one who gives freely)
key_terms.تَعَلَّقَ: Held fast to / attached oneself to

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of generosity in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the virtue of generosity (sakha') to both divine closeness and social harmony, emphasizing its role in fostering community bonds. The metaphor of the 'tree in Paradise' underscores generosity not merely as a moral act but as a spiritual anchor that guarantees eternal reward, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on character refinement (akhlaq).

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The generous one is close to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, close to the Paradise, and close to the people’. And I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The generosity is a tree in the Paradise. The one who attaches himself in one of its branches would enter the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 9. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ who has said the following: “

I heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘A generous person is close to Allah, close to Paradise and close to people.’ I also heard him say, ‘Generosity is a tree in Paradise. Whoever holds to one of its branches will enter Paradise.’”
